root.name: Benoni Defense: Taimanov Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 e6 4. Nc3 exd5 5. cxd5 d6 6. e4 g6 7. f4 Bg7 8. Bb5+

overview: A branch of the Four Pawns Attack against the Modern Benoni. White checks with 8.Bb5+, Black blocks with 8...Nfd7 (the input's main line), and play continues 9.a4 O-O 10.Nf3 with the Zaitsev set-up, or 9.Bd3. White has a big pawn centre with e4-e5 threats; Black aims for ...Na6, ...Nb6 and ...c4 or ...b5 breaks and pressure on the e-file. Both sides take large risks and theory is deep.

white_ideas.idea: Support the e4-e5 break with Nf3, O-O and a4, and use the centre space and attack on the kingside.
Play for e5 and use the bishop on b5 to restrain ...a6 and ...b5.

black_ideas.idea: Block with ...Nfd7, castle and reposition the knight with ...Na6-c7 and aim for ...b5.
Strike with ...c4 or ...Re8 to exploit the e-file and the weak d4 and e5 squares.

typical_structures.structure: Four Pawns centre of c-pawn gone, d5, e4, f4 against Black's c5/d6 and a half-open e-file.

character.notes: A pawn centre against active counterplay; one slip in the e4-e5 timing or ...b5 breaks loses quickly, so the play is sharp.

gambit.notes: No material is offered in the main line.

soundness.notes: Established Benoni line with deep theory; both sides are sound.

structure.notes: A fixed asymmetric centre with Black's half-open e-file, which is semi-open by the rubric.

approach.notes: A mainstream Benoni sub-line chosen by strong players.

level.notes: The Four Pawns lines are long and forcing, so Black must know the theory.
